utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, will you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case IT-95-8/1-I, the Prosecutor versus Nenad Banovic and Predrag Banovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the parties present themselves, please. Can we have the appearances for the Prosecution first?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Dirk Ryneveld along with Nicholas Koumjian for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I am Jelena Nikolic, attorney from Novi Sad, Yugoslavia, representing the Defence of Mr. Nenad Banovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm Tomslav Visnjic, attorney representing Mr. Predrag Banovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nenad Banovic and Mr. Predrag Banovic, will you please rise. Can you follow the hearing in a language that you understand? THE ACCUSED N. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nenad Banovic, will you please tell us your name, first name, age, and occupation. THE ACCUSED N. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] I was born on the 28th of October, 1969, in Prijedor, and I am a catering worker, and my name is Nenad Banovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Predrag Banovic, please, will you introduce yourself. THE ACCUSED P. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] I was born on the 28th of October, 1969, in Prijedor. I am also a catering worker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. This is your initial appearance before the Tribunal. This formality is of essential importance, and on this occasion, you will be able to hear the charges which the Prosecutor has pressed against you. Have you received the indictment, Mr. Nenad? Have you received the indictment? THE ACCUSED N. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you, Mr. Predrag, have you received the indictment? THE ACCUSED P. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you spoken to your attorneys? Do you want the indictment to be read out in its entirety in this courtroom? This is a right that you may use, or you may waive this right. Mr. Nenad, do you want the whole indictment to be read out to you or not? THE ACCUSED N. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Predrag? THE ACCUSED P. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I take note that both of you have waived this right. We are now proceeding to the main event of this initial appearance, and that is your -- whether you intend to plead guilty or not guilty to the charges against you, unless you prefer to do so within a time period of 30 days. So have you understood? You can plead guilty or not guilty today, but you may also request to have a time period of 30 days to make that plea. Which do you prefer, to plead today or later? We are now going to read out the charges against you, upon which you will tell us whether you plead guilty or not guilty. Madam Registrar, will you please read the charges?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Second Amended Indictment: The accused, Nenad Banovic, also known as Bani, born on the 28th of October, 1969, in Prijedor, Bosnia-Herzegovina. Prior to the conflict, he worked as a waiter. He regularly performed duties as a guard at the Keraterm camp and participated in the abusing, beating, torturing and/or killing detainees in the Keraterm camp. Predrag Banovic, also known as Cupo, born on the 28th of October, 1969, in Prijedor, Bosnia-Herzegovina. Prior to the conflict, he worked as a waiter. He regularly performed duties as a guard at the Keraterm camp and participated in abusing, beating, torturing and/or killing detainees in the Keraterm camp. The charges. Counts 3 to 5: Persecutions, inhuman acts, and outrages upon personal dignity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you plead guilty or not guilty of these charges? THE ACCUSED P. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you, please? THE ACCUSED N. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone was not on. Could you switch on the microphone, please? THE ACCUSED N. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sit down, please. Will you continue reading with the other counts, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Counts 16 to 22. Predrag Banovic, Count 16, murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 17, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 18, torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(f) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 19, torture, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 20, inhuman acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 21, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Predrag Banovic, Predrag, will you rise, please? How do you plead to these counts that have been read out to you by Madam Registrar? THE ACCUSED P. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sit down. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Counts 23 to 26. Predrag Banovic, Count 23, murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 24, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; or, in the alternative, Count 25, inhuman acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 26, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Predrag Banovic, rise again, please. How do you plead? THE ACCUSED P. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sit down. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counts 27 to 32. Predrag Banovic, Nenad Banovic: Count 27, murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 28, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; or in the alternative, Count 29, torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(f) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 30, torture, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 31, inhuman acts, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 32, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Predrag Banovic. THE ACCUSED P. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sit down. Nenad Banovic. THE ACCUSED N. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not feel guilty under any of the counts of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We take note of that. Sit down. Continue, madam.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counts 37 to 42. Predrag Banovic: Count 37, murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 38, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 39, torture, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(f) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 40, torture, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 41, inhuman acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; and Count 42, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Predrag Banovic, please rise. How do you plead? THE ACCUSED P. BANOVIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sit down. Madam Registrar, will you take note of the replies of the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, I wish to remind you of your obligations under Article 66(1) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, that is, the disclosure of supporting material within a time period of 30 days. I also wish to address the Defence, to remind them of Rule 62 of the Rules, which says that preliminary motions may be filed within a period of 30 days. Have you taken note of that? Under Rule 72. I'm sorry. I wish to underline that this case has been attributed to Chamber III by order of the President and that a Pre-Trial Judge will be designated shortly. Do you have anything to raise, madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one point, Your Honour. As the attorney for Nenad Banovic, I have just been provisionally appointed for this initial appearance because of the obligations under Rule 62.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I take note of that, madam. Have you anything to observe, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have the same observation to make. In view of our provisional status and the obligations of the Prosecution regarding discovery will be carried out probably with the cooperation of the attorneys who will be appointed as permanent Defence counsel for these defendants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just two brief matters, if I may, more by way of advice, as a courtesy to the Court and to my learned friends that the Prosecution is intending to amend the existing indictment for two reasons: One, in order to make it a more precise consist document. Three of the seven names currently on the indictment, as you know, have already been through a trial process, and so we would make this a document that's more in keeping with the two accused who are presently before the Court. And secondly, in light of the recent judgement concerning Messrs. Sikirica, Dosen, and Kolundzija, the Prosecution will also be amending its indictment in order to be in conformity with both the law and the facts as decided in that case. So I'm just advising the Court, as a courtesy, that we will in due course be filing an amended indictment. At least that is our -- that will be our application. Secondly, I just want to indicate to the Court, you have reminded us of our obligations under 66(A)(i). We will, in fact, have the supporting material available for disclosure to the Defence within 30 days. However, I do anticipate bringing on a motion, a written motion in the future, before the 30 days, with respect to the right to redact the names of some protected witnesses, and I've told my friends of our intention to do that. So the Court will be getting a motion. Because of the unique circumstances in this case, we want to bring on a motion that will basically redact the names of the same witnesses from the supporting material only as were ordered in previous proceedings. So those are the only issues, by way of a courtesy, I want to bring to the attention of both the Court and my learned friends. Those are the issues on behalf of the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has been duly informed about all these matters, both about this stage of the proceedings and in the status that I have as representative of Nenad Banovic, we have agreed. As for the future, the permanent Defence counsel will be in communication with the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I take note of all this, and I think that the Pre-Trial Judge will clarify these things further, because this hearing devoted to the initial appearance is thus over. Before adjourning, I wish to thank the interpreters and the technical staff for their cooperation and their efficiency. The hearing is adjourned.
